title: Economics-first recommendations UX — sprint notes
body:
Context
-----
Sprint-level working notes for an economics-first UX for Optimize recommendations. Aim: make batching/caching/quantization suggestions actionable and explorable by engineers and platform owners, with immediate cost impact visibility and quality tradeoff signals. This doc captures wireframe ideas, micro-interactions, backlog candidates, and acceptance criteria for a 2-week spike. Mostly rough notes and TODOs — iterate in pairing sessions with SRE and applied-ml.

Summary of goals
- Surface recommended levers (batch_size, prefix_cache, kv_cache_ttl, quant_profile) as prescriptive cards.
- Show estimated cost delta (tokens/sec cost and $/M tokens) and expected latency change.
- Provide a quick "simulate" panel that runs on sampled trace to estimate quality/regression risk and latency distribution.
- Enable one-click apply to route or create a canary rollout.
- Add explainers for quantization accuracy risk and suggested guardrails (per-model test prompts).

Wireframe notes (low-fi)
1) Recommendations Canvas (left column)
   - Top: route selector (dropdown, search).
   - Below: visual stack of "Active config" (current batching + cache + model variant) as a compact card.
   - Middle area: Recommendation cards stacked vertically. Each card shows: title (e.g., "Enable prefix caching"), short rationale, primary metric row (delta cost, delta p50 latency), confidence badge (high/medium/low), and action buttons: "Preview", "Apply to route", "Create canary".
   - Microcopy: "Estimated savings based on last 72h of traffic" with a small ? icon.

2) Right-side Inspector / Simulator panel
   - Tabs: Overview | Latency impact | Quality checks | Trace samples.
   - Overview shows baseline vs post-change: cost, p50/p95 latency, token throughput. Small sparkline for trend.
   - Latency impact: histogram heatmap of latencies (sampled). Toggle options: include warmup KV cache / cold start.
   - Quality checks: run a cheap eval subset (100 prompts) with a golden set and show EM/QA diffs; flag examples with changed outputs. "Risk" score 0-100.

3) Interaction flows
   - Preview: compute a lightweight simulation (client-side + server sample job). If heavy, show estimate and queue job for full sim.
   - Apply to route: prompts a modal with staging options: immediate apply, canary (10% traffic for 1h), or schedule. Show rollback button and link to rollout audit.
   - Quick revert: a soft rollback (auto-apply fallback to previous variant if 5xx or latency > threshold).

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- UI displays top 3 automated recommendations for selected route with estimated cost and latency impact.
- Simulator returns a quick estimate (<=15s) on sampled traffic for the selected route.
- "Apply to route" triggers a canary rollout and records action in audit logs.
- Basic quality checks run against a submitted prompt set and surface at least 3 changed examples when quantization is suggested.

Backlog / TODO (prioritized)
P0
- Hook recommendations engine (backend) -> UI endpoint returning recommendations and cost deltas (OPT-412).
- Basic simulator endpoint that runs a 100-sample pass and returns latency histogram + diff examples.
- Action endpoint for canary rollout with audit entry.

P1
- Inline what-if slider for batch_size and max_batch_latency to see effect in realtime.
- Support per-model quantization presets + preview of size/throughput gains.
- Confidence scoring: train simple heuristic using historical change regressions.

P2
- Multi-route bulk apply workflow (apply same preset across selected routes).
- Auto-suggestions for TTL based on route traffic rhythms (to avoid stale cache thrash).

Open questions / risks
- Simulation cost: full sim for high-traffic routes is expensive. Need sampling heuristics or offline jobs. Tradeoff: faster but less accurate estimates vs queued background jobs.
- Quantization quality signal: for many models even 8-bit quant can change subtle outputs. Need a UX to surface example diffs and fallback to unquantized for critical routes.
- Ownership model for "apply": who can apply changes? Devs vs platform? Need RBAC mapping with Console team.
- Metric drift: recommendations based on last 72h may be stale for seasonally spiky routes. Consider option to choose time window.

Microcopy / labels ideas
- Card CTA: "Preview impact" (not "Simulate" to avoid heavy connotation)
- Confidence/why: small line: "Based on Xk requests, typical seq len Y"
- Risk tooltip: "Quality risk estimates are approximate. Run full eval for high-sensitivity routes."

Design constraints
- Keep cards compact to allow scanning many recommendations.
- Use color coding where green = cost down, orange = latency up. Put risk icons separately to avoid alarm fatigue.
- Ensure keyboard accessibility for bulk apply flows.

Metrics to monitor after launch
- Acceptance/Adoption: percent of recommendations previewed, percent applied, canary success rate.
- Unit economics: estimated $/month saved from applied suggestions.
- Quality regressions: number of canaries that trigger rollbacks due to quality.
- Simulation latency: median time to preview result.

Notes to self / next steps
- Pair with Ethan and Miguel to scope recommended API response shape (include fields: id, kind, estimate_cost_delta, estimate_latency_delta, confidence, suggested_params, sample_trace_id).
- Design session with Rina to make low-fi mocks + accessible color palette.
- Draft copy for tooltips and audit log entries.

Appendix: example mock JSON response (sketch) "id: rec-309", "kind: prefix_cache", "estimate_cost_delta: "-12%"", "estimate_latency_delta: "-8ms p50"", "confidence: high"   // keep actual schema in API doc

References
- Related drive docs: optimize-recs-inspector-flow-annotated-wip, inference-prescriptor-playbook-wip (for playbook language).
- Backend work: JIRA-OPT-412 (recommendation endpoint), infra ticket SRE-68 (sim sampler).

-- end --
